recall.minute: Policy-based methods parameterise π(a|s, θ) (softmax over preferences for discrete actions, Gaussian for continuous) and ascend performance J(θ). Advantages: continuous actions, stochastic optimal policies (short corridor: P(right) ≈ 0.59 gives −11.6 while deterministic policies never finish), smooth policy changes; disadvantages: high variance, local optima, sample inefficiency. The policy gradient theorem gives ∇J ∝ E[q(S, A)∇ln π(A|S)] via the log-derivative trick. REINFORCE uses Gₜ: θ = [0.5, −0.2], π = (0.668, 0.332), G = 2, α = 0.1 → [0.566, −0.266]. Action-independent baselines leave the gradient unbiased and cut variance; with v̂(s) they yield advantage estimates. Actor–critic uses the critic's TD error δ for online updates (A2C/A3C, n-step, GAE). Natural gradients use the Fisher matrix; TRPO constrains KL; PPO clips the ratio (r = 1.3, A = 3, ε = 0.2 → 3.6). DDPG (deterministic actor), TD3 (twin critics, delayed updates, target smoothing) and SAC (maximum entropy) handle continuous control off-policy.
